content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge resolves the D5/C1 collision by citing how the pressed verses and answers are worded, so it is doing the chain-versus-chain weighing governed by K-C.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse — I weighed whether it forbids deciding by the absence of an explicit statement in the verse's own words, or only forbids counting a verse's silence as contrary proof while allowing silence to be noted within chain footing.", "why": "Because the judge decides underdetermination from the absence of an explicit naming in the text, it uses a verse-level wording test instead of weighing the competing chains by footing as K-C requires."}
